---
applyTo: '**/*.md'
---

# Rules for .md files

Each rule cites the code it rests on. A rule marked not yet reviewed is the estate's best reading, not a decision.

- [Invariant] Client error responses must return RFC 9457 problem details and must never expose internal stack traces or exception messages to clients. [SECURITY.md:L14-L14]
- [ArchitectureDecision] Adopt the Result pattern and RFC 9457 problem details: the domain returns Result / Result<T> carrying Error(Code, Description, Type); Claim.Declare returns all violated rules at once; ResultExtensions.ToProblem maps errors to RFC 9457 problem details (Validation -> 400 ValidationProblem keyed by stable code, NotFound -> 404, Conflict -> 409 with a code extension); successful responses return the resource directly without an envelope; unexpected exceptions are routed to UnhandledExceptionHandler to return a generic 500 logged with a trace ID and never expose stack traces. [docs/adr/0005-result-pattern-problem-details.md:L1-L26]
- [ArchitectureDecision] Aggregates buffer domain events via AggregateRoot.Raise. DomainEventsToOutboxInterceptor persists them into outbox_messages rows inside the same database transaction as the state change. OutboxProcessor<TDbContext> (a BackgroundService) claims pending rows using SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, dispatches them to IDomainEventHandler<T> implementations, marks them processed, and retries failures up to 5 times while storing the error on the row. Event types are resolved through a closed registry (OutboxEventRegistry) rather than Type.GetType(row.Type). [docs/adr/0002-transactional-outbox.md:L1-L29]
- [ArchitectureDecision] Angular 22 zoneless with OnPush standalone components; reads via httpResource and commands via ClaimsApi; Signal Forms for client declarations; subscriptionless realtime via SignalR signals triggering reloadWhen/reload(); server-driven workflow via allowedActions; and built-in Angular i18n with separate compiled builds per language. Hub connection injected via InjectionToken factory. [docs/adr/0007-frontend-signals-server-driven-workflow.md:L1-L24]
- [ArchitectureDecision] - PostgreSQL (via Npgsql EF Core provider): jsonb for outbox payloads, partial indexes, SKIP LOCKED. - Optimistic concurrency on the xmin system column (Version mapped with IsRowVersion()): no extra column, PostgreSQL bumps it on every update. - The API returns version with every claim; a command must send back the expectedVersion it was based on. ApplyClaimAction sets it as the original value, so a stale command fails with 409 claim.concurrent_update and the UI reloads the fresh state. - Migrations: applied at startup only when Database:InitializeOnStartup is true (local, tests, demo). For production the CI produces a self-contained EF migration bundle (efbundle artifact) that runs as a pipeline step before the new version receives traffic — the app never needs DDL rights at runtime. - Claim numbers (SIN-2026-000123) come from a PostgreSQL sequence (claims.claim_number_seq): unique across concurrent transactions by construction. A rolled-back declaration leaves a gap, which a business reference tolerates. [docs/adr/0003-postgresql-optimistic-concurrency.md:L1-L26]
- [ArchitectureDecision] No retrieval and no vector store: the entire file (<= 12 documents, <= 24 MB per request) is sent in one call to Claude (claude-opus-5-5, effort medium) via Anthropic .NET SDK. PDFs are sent natively with citations enabled, formatted by AnalysisComposer as footnote citations ([[n]]) linked to page-level source passages. The system is advisory only with no write access/tools; reviews are stored in the audit trail with requester, model, document count, and token usage; cost guardrails include 6 reviews/hour per-user rate limit, request size budgets, and fallback configuration; and IClaimAnalyst acts as the test seam with deterministic fakes in CI. [docs/adr/0009-ai-file-review-with-citations.md:L1-L34]
- [ArchitectureDecision] Adopt a multi-layer testing strategy: unit tests with xUnit v3 and Shouldly for domain workflows and invariants; NetArchTest for architectural module boundaries; WebApplicationFactory with Testcontainers PostgreSQL 18 for integration tests; Vitest for frontend; tests executed via Microsoft.Testing.Platform; and an 80% line coverage gate in CI. [docs/adr/0006-testing-strategy.md:L1-L24]
- [ArchitectureDecision] The API acts as an OAuth 2.0 resource server validating JWT bearer tokens with standard OIDC claims (sub, name, role; MapInboundClaims = false) supporting Oidc mode (default, validating against provider JWKS via Authority) and Demo mode (built-in /api/auth/token endpoint with 4 personas using an HMAC secret). Authorization is split into module role-based policies (claims.read, claims.write) and domain rules (delegated authority limits and the four-eyes principle on settlement), returning caller-tailored allowedActions. [docs/adr/0008-authentication-and-segregation-of-duties.md:L1-L45]
- [ArchitectureDecision] Feature handlers use ClaimsDbContext directly. Read endpoints project straight to response DTOs with AsNoTracking().Select(...); write endpoints load the aggregate, call a domain method, and save. [docs/adr/0004-no-repository-over-dbcontext.md:L1-L20]
- [InformalDecision] Authorization is enforced via module-declared policies combined with domain business rules, including delegated financial limits and four-eyes review controls. [SECURITY.md:L9-L9]
- [InformalDecision] Authentication relies on OIDC-compatible JWT bearer tokens, and authentication configuration options are validated at application startup. [SECURITY.md:L8-L8]
- [InformalDecision] Uploaded files are stored in a private blob container and served only after authorization, scoped specifically by claim ID. [SECURITY.md:L11-L11]
- [InformalDecision] Abuse mitigation is enforced using per-IP rate limiting across the API and SignalR hub, and per-user budget quotas on AI file reviews. [SECURITY.md:L12-L12]
- [InformalDecision] API responses enforce secure HTTP headers including nosniff content-type options, DENY framing options, no-referrer policy, and a strict Content Security Policy. [SECURITY.md:L15-L15]
- [InformalDecision] Input validation uses domain Result rules, serializes enums as names only, sniffs file upload content for valid MIME types, and sanitizes uploaded file names. [SECURITY.md:L10-L10]
- [InformalDecision] No secrets are committed to the repository; secrets are provisioned via user-secrets and Aspire-generated parameters in local development, and Azure Container Apps secrets in production. [SECURITY.md:L17-L17]
- [InformalDecision] AI integration treats document contents as untrusted input with prompt-injection guards, and designates all AI review outputs as advisory only. [SECURITY.md:L13-L13]
- [InformalDecision] Supply chain security is managed using central package management, Dependabot automated updates, CodeQL static analysis, and vulnerable-package audits in CI. [SECURITY.md:L16-L16]
